chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Take (remove) hair from yourself when you intend for the Hajj, the entire month of Shawwal until the first ten days of Dhu al-Qi'dah."

key_terms.الشَّوَّال: Shawwal (the 10th month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhu al-Qi'dah (the 11th month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.شَعْر: Hair (specifically body hair, often referring to underarm or pubic hair in the context of Ihram preparation)
key_terms.غُرَّة: The first ten days (of a month)

ai.seo_question: When should one begin removing hair before Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the preparatory phase of Hajj by linking the removal of hair to the intention (Izmir) rather than a fixed calendar start, extending the permissibility through Shawwal until the first of Dhu al-Qi'dah. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the flexibility in pre-Hajj rituals, distinguishing between the act of entering Ihram and the preliminary grooming that can occur earlier. It underscores the scholarly emphasis on the pilgrim's internal state of intention as the trigger for these preparatory obligations.
